query: For an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating susceptible to progressive plastic deformation during continuous loading, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its creep resistance? Specify the governing factor and rationale, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, the operating boundaries under sustained stress, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The superior creep resistance of dual-phase FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy (HEA) protective coatings arises because severe, compositionally driven lattice distortion in the solid solution reduces the effective vacancy mobility and therefore suppresses dislocation climb; the governing factor is an increase (≥40 %) in the apparent activation energy for self-diffusion relative to compositionally simpler alloys of the same crystal structure.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited or homogenized ~30 µm thick equiatomic (e.g., Al0.3CoCrFeNi) FCC/BCC nanocrystalline coating, grain size 50–150 nm, no secondary precipitates, residual stress <50 MPa, surface roughness Ra <0.2 µm.
generation.intervention: Apply constant uniaxial (or bending) stress equal to 60 % of the 0.2 % yield strength at temperatures 0.35–0.50 Tm for up to 100 h.
generation.conditions: High-vacuum (<10-5 mbar) or inert Ar atmosphere; temperature steps 0.35, 0.40, 0.45, 0.50 Tm; stress held constant ±1 %.
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic-scale lattice distortion fields around the chemically disordered sites that increase the energy barrier for vacancy migration and hinder dislocation climb.
generation.mechanism:
1) Random occupation of lattice sites by elements with large size and modulus misfit produces long-range elastic fields (‘severe lattice distortion’).
2) Vacancy formation and migration require higher local energy, elevating the activation energy (Q) for self-diffusion.
3) Dislocation climb—rate-controlling for high-temperature creep—slows markedly; dislocations accumulate and tangle instead of bypassing obstacles.
4) The coating therefore sustains load with minimal plastic strain accumulation over time.
generation.predicted_outcome:
Relative to a binary Ni-Fe or pure-Ni reference coating tested identically,
• The HEA will show 1–2 orders of magnitude lower steady-state creep rate (ϵ̇_ss) at every test temperature.
• Arrhenius plots of ln ϵ̇_ss vs 1/T will yield an apparent activation energy Q at least 40 % higher than the reference.
• Post-creep TEM will reveal high densities of sessile/tangled dislocations with scarce climb ledges; the reference will show extensive climb dipoles and subgrain formation.
generation.baseline: Creep behaviour of single-phase FCC Ni or binary Ni-Fe coating fabricated and tested under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: Advantage expected up to ≈0.5 Tm and stresses ≤0.7 σ0.2; above these, enhanced diffusion or dynamic recrystallisation may restore ordinary creep rates and invalidate the mechanism.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative size of the Q increase (assumed ≥40 %) and the exact stress exponent may vary with precise composition and grain size; grain-boundary diffusion in very fine-grained coatings could add competing mechanisms.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two coatings: (A) the HEA described above, (B) reference Ni-Fe (50/50 at. %) with similar grain size and hardness. Conduct constant-load creep tests at 0.40 Tm for 100 h and temperature-ramp creep (0.35–0.50 Tm) to build Arrhenius plots. Examine microstructure pre- and post-test by TEM and atom-probe tomography.
measurements: Steady-state creep rate ϵ̇_ss vs time
Activation energy Q from ln ϵ̇ vs 1/T
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEA’s activation energy for creep (Q_HEA) is not at least 20 % higher than Q_reference OR its steady-state creep rate is less than one half-order of magnitude lower than the reference under every tested condition, OR TEM shows comparable extent of dislocation climb features, then the hypothesis is falsified.
